text: A magistrate issued summons against me in a cheating complaint filed by a company without really looking at the facts. Can the High Court cancel the summons?
Scope of the High Court's power to quash a summoning order passed mechanically by a Magistrate, and what the Magistrate must show before issuing process.
Can a company be prosecuted for an offence when the law says the punishment is jail and fine, but a company cannot be put in jail?
Whether a corporate entity can be prosecuted for an offence where imprisonment and fine are both mandatory, and what sentence can be imposed on it.
A company was accused of cheating through its directors. Can the company itself be treated as a criminal accused, or only the people?
Attribution of the mens rea of directors to the company for offences requiring intent such as cheating, and the company's amenability to prosecution.
The police want to prosecute the directors of a company for what the company did. When is a director personally criminally responsible?
Vicarious criminal liability of directors for company offences and the 'alter ego' doctrine; conditions for summoning directors as accused.
I am only a director of a company and was named in a cheating case. Can I be dragged into the case just because I am a director?
Quashing of proceedings against a director where the complaint does not attribute any specific role to him in the company's offence.
In a cheque bounce case against a company, the complaint names me as a director but does not say what my role was. Can I be held liable?
Section 141 Negotiable Instruments Act: sufficiency of averments in the complaint that a director was in charge of and responsible for the company's business.
My cheque bounce case is pending for years. Can the case be settled with the person who gave me the cheque even now, and does it get closed?
Compounding of the offence under Section 138 at any stage, guidelines for summary trial and the court's power to impose costs on a non-consenting complainant.
A business deal went wrong and the other side filed a cheating case instead of a civil suit for money. Can I ask the court to throw out the criminal case?
Quashing of criminal proceedings that give a criminal colour to what is essentially a civil or commercial dispute; the principles for exercising inherent power.
Our contract has an arbitration clause. The other party still filed a criminal complaint for cheating. Does the arbitration clause stop the criminal case?
Whether the existence of an arbitration clause bars criminal proceedings for cheating and criminal breach of trust arising out of the same transaction.
A property dealing dispute between two companies became a criminal case. Can the High Court close it when the matter is basically civil?
Quashing under the High Court's inherent power where the dispute is predominantly civil, and the relevance of settlement between the parties.
My FIR is clearly false and was filed to harass me. In what situations can the High Court cancel an FIR before the police finish investigation?
The categories of cases in which the High Court may quash an FIR or complaint in exercise of its inherent powers to prevent abuse of process.
I want the High Court to quash a case against me. Can I give my own documents showing I am innocent, or does the court only look at the police papers?
The approach of the High Court in a quashing petition: whether the accused's defence material can be considered and the steps of the test.
In a cheque bounce case, do I have to prove that I did not owe the money, or does the other person have to prove that the cheque was for a real debt?
Presumption under Sections 118 and 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in favour of the holder and the burden on the drawer to rebut.
How much must a person prove to show that a cheque was not given for a debt? Is it as strict as proving a crime?
The standard of proof for rebutting the presumption under Section 139: preponderance of probabilities and not proof beyond reasonable doubt.
My neighbour filed a criminal case over a money dispute to put pressure on me. Can a court stop criminal proceedings that are really about a civil debt?
Criminal proceedings initiated to settle civil scores: the duty of the court to examine whether the complaint discloses an offence before taking cognizance.
We have settled our dispute. Can a criminal case that is not normally compoundable be closed because both sides agreed?
Power of the High Court under Section 482 to quash non-compoundable offences on settlement and its distinction from compounding under Section 320.
Does a magistrate have to give a detailed reason when he decides to take a case forward and issue summons to me?
Whether a summoning order must record detailed reasons and what application of mind the Magistrate must show at the stage of taking cognizance.
